# AGENTS.md — test/fixtures/

Read [`../../AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md) first. Active fixture work belongs only
in sibling `PLAN.md`; load it only when changing this directory.

Small `.ifc` files for use in crate tests: mostly copied from upstream
reference repos, plus one generated set (see `synthetic-surfaces/`).
Total ~432 KiB, 32 files —
kept intentionally small; this is a curated edge-case set, not a bulk corpus.

## Layout

- `ifclite-geometry/` — 14 files from `ifc-lite`'s
  `rust/geometry/tests/fixtures/` and `rust/processing/tests/fixtures/`
  (MPL-2.0, github.com/LTplus-AG/ifc-lite). Geometry edge cases: mapped-item
  cycles/nesting, swept-disk composite-curve profiles, shared-point faceted
  breps, CSG, halfspace flyaway, scaled units, overlapping wall openings,
  and (`mapped_instances_indexed_colour*.ifc`) IFC4 triangulated face sets with
  an indexed colour map. `issue_1485_duct_elbow_surface_curve_swept.ifc` is a
  round duct elbow: a profile swept along a trimmed arc that lies on an
  `IfcSurfaceOfLinearExtrusion`, and the only fixture carrying a non-planar
  surface construction.
  Filenames match upstream (`issue_NNNN_*`, `mapped_instances_*`,
  `swept_disk_*`) — keep that convention when adding more so provenance stays
  traceable by name alone.
- `synthetic-surfaces/` — 9 files GENERATED by
  [`../../tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py`](../../tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py)
  using ifcopenshell 0.8.5. **Not sourced from any upstream corpus**, and that
  is deliberate: no licensed public corpus we surveyed carries curved or
  B-spline surfaces at all. `ifc-lite` (MPL-2.0) has none; the buildingSMART
  sets (CC-BY-4.0) contain only faceted breps and extrusions; the one repo that
  does have them, `IfcOpenShell/files`, publishes **no licence**, so its files
  cannot be redistributed here. Generating our own is the only route that is
  both licence-clean and committable.

  Covers `IfcCylindricalSurface`, `IfcSphericalSurface`, `IfcToroidalSurface`,
  `IfcSurfaceOfRevolution`, `IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface`,
  `IfcBSplineSurfaceWithKnots`, and `IfcCurveBoundedPlane`, plus
  `IfcAdvancedBrep` (`synthetic_advanced_brep.ifc`: a half-cylinder plug whose
  three faces share four edges through eight `IfcOrientedEdge` uses, with one
  `IfcEdgeCurve` and one `IfcAdvancedFace` authored `SameSense=.F.` so a
  dropped flag is observable), `IfcRectangularPyramid` and
  `IfcBoundingBox` (`synthetic_primitives_and_bbox.ifc`: three distinct
  extents, so a slot-order mistake cannot pass), and the loose collections
  (`synthetic_collections.ifc`: a curve set of a polyline plus a circle, and
  a shell-based surface model of two triangles in an OPEN shell — it must
  never acquire a volume), the tapered and variable-section sweeps
  (`synthetic_tapered_sweeps.ifc`: every tapered pair uses DISTINCT start and
  end profiles so reusing `SweptArea` for both ends is observable, the
  revolution angle is authored in degrees, the fixed reference is `+Z` rather
  than the `+X` a lowerer would default to, and the polygonal disk appears
  BOTH with and without `FilletRadius` because only the unfilleted case
  lowers), and `IfcSectionedSpine` (`synthetic_sectioned_spine.ifc`: three
  different profiles at three distinct stations along a composite curve).
  All are authored in
  **millimetres with degree angles** — the combination that catches a unit
  factor applied to the wrong quantity kind — and every file passes
  `ifcopenshell.validate` with zero issues.

  Regenerate with:

  ```
  python3 tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py test/fixtures/synthetic-surfaces
  ```

  Edit the generator, never the `.ifc` output: the script is the source of
  truth and records why each value was chosen (e.g. the revolution axis sits
  off-origin so a missing millimetre conversion cannot hide).

- `ifcopenshell-validate/` — 8 files from `ifcopenshell`'s
  `src/ifcopenshell-python/test/fixtures/validate/` (LGPL-3.0-or-later,
  github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell). Schema/header validation edge cases:
  `pass-*` / `fail-*` pairs for duplicated GUIDs, selected simple types,
  complex numbers, malformed headers. These are IFC-spec-conformance cases,
  not geometry.

## Agent rules

1. **These are third-party test data.** Preserve upstream provenance and license
   terms; do not add a fixture that looks like a real client export rather than
   a synthetic/minimal repro case.
2. **Keep the `pass-`/`fail-`/`issue_NNNN_` naming from upstream** when you add
   more files from the same source — it's how you trace a fixture back to the
   upstream test it validates without a separate manifest.
3. **Add new fixtures deliberately, not in bulk.** The point of this directory
   is edge-case coverage per IFC construct, not corpus size. Before adding a
   new file, check it actually exercises something the existing 20 don't.
4. When a crate test loads one of these, reference it by relative path from
   the crate (`../test/fixtures/<subdir>/<file>.ifc`) and name the test
   after the fixture so a failing test is self-describing.
5. Full oracle-scale `.ifc` corpora (e.g. Solibri's example models) belong to
   external local oracle storage, not here — this repo's fixtures stay
   small and hand-picked.
